newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish biker murder trial opens.
newsitem.headline: Danish biker murder trial opens.

text.p: Six members and associates of the Hell's Angels bike gang went on trial on Monday, amid the tightest security measures seen in a Danish court, accused of killing a rival in an airport shooting.

The March 10 incident turned a festering vendetta between the Hell's Angels and the Bandidos gang into full-blooded war in which the rivals have blasted each other with machine-guns, hand grenades, bombs and anti-tank missiles across the Nordic region.
The prosecution says the six accused, four Hell's Angels members and two associates, jointly planned the Copenhagen airport attack and are all guilty, regardless of who fired the shots.

Police, who have long struggled to prove that the gangs are organised criminal rings rather than groupings of errant individuals, hope evidence arising during the proceedings will confirm their claim.
"We shall see...if we can have the theory that the groups carry out organised crime, steered from the top, proved or disproved," Detective Chief Inspector Per Larsen told the Politiken daily.
At the courtroom on Monday spectators were screened by metal detector and scrutinised by officers familiar with biker gangs.
Police bomb experts swept the court before the opening session and will do so before each sitting.
Cleaning staff have been specially vetted and were watched by police as they worked.
The biker feud claimed its first life in February 1994, when a member of the Hell's Angels-affiliated Rednecks died in a gunfight with Bandidos in the Swedish port of Helsingborg.
Two more Bandidos died over the following two years, in Sweden and in Finland. But the airport incident in March injected new intensity into the bitter feuding.

Gunmen outside Copenhagen International airport shot dead Danish Bandidos leader Uffe Larsen and wounded three of his companions as they waited to meet fellow-members returning from a visit to Helsinki.
At almost the same time, in Norway, an attacker shot and wounded a Bandido arriving at Oslo's Fornebu airport. Police arrested a member of a Hell's Angels-allied gang.
Since then the weapons used have become heavier, three more people have died and others have been maimed.
The Copenhagen trial, expected to take up to six weeks, is complicated by the silence of witnesses.

Bystanders are terrified to give evidence for fear of reprisals, while those within the biker fraternity are bound by a code forbidding cooperation with the police. Even the surviving victims refuse to identify their attackers.
